This confirms C6 is checking for a specific commitment structure (a separate signal-shop/UPS-vendor coordination assignment) that rollouts 1 and 2 folded into a generic calendar_publication or crew_assignment commitment. P1 failed in 1 of 4 rollouts (tally 3/4). In rollout 0, PF2 was never revealed and not cited in justification_fact_ids, so P1 fails as NEVER REVEALED — A3 said 'Wednesday afternoon' in a say action but never issued a reveal for PF2, and the settlement only credited PF1. C3 and C4 each failed in 1 of 4 rollouts (tally 3/4 each). In rollout 0, PF2 was never revealed, so both fail as NEVER REVEALED. No turn-cap auto-fails occurred; all 4 rollouts settled within 3-6 turns. C6 (ENCODING MISMATCH, rollouts 1-2): Loosen check C6 to accept coordination evidence from either a dedicated assign_support/coordination commitment targeting 'signal shop' OR a calendar_publication/crew_assignment commitment whose detail text mentions both the UPS test window (1300-1500) and the generator-transfer test (1500-1530) with signal shop presence. The exact new wording should match on commitment detail text containing 'signal shop' (or 'signal-shop') AND 'generator-transfer' (or 'transfer test'), regardless of commitment type. Flag: this does NOT risk LEAKED regression because the 1300-1500 and 1500-1530 windows with signal shop presence are only knowable from PF2. 3. P1 (NEVER REVEALED, rollout 0): Add a shared_context sentence requiring that each agent must issue a formal reveal action for their decisive fact before the convener can settle — e.g., 'The convener must not publish the final calendar until every section lead has formally revealed their current constraint via a reveal action, not merely mentioned it in discussion.' This prevents A3 from substituting a 'say' for a 'reveal' and prevents A1 from settling prematurely. 4. C3 and C4 (NEVER REVEALED, rollout 0): Same fix as P1 — the shared_context reveal-before-settle norm will ensure PF2 is formally disclosed, which will make C3 and C4 passable.
